newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR STABLE BUT PRESSURE STILL ON.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR STABLE BUT PRESSURE STILL ON.

text.p: The Zimbabwe dollar was trading little changed from Thursday's closing levels against the key U.S. dollar early on Friday but dealers said import pressure still persisted and predicted the local unit would resume its fall.

"Our market has been in turmoil for the past three days and there's still a big shortage in the market," one dealer said, adding that the central Reserve Bank was still standing mostly aloof and allowing the dollar to depreciate.

In an interview with the private-owned Financial Gazette newspaper published on Friday, Reserve Bank governor Leonard Tsumba said the Zimbabwe dollar was overvalued by five percent and hinted the bank would allow it to depreciate further in order to maintain export competivemess.
"But we don't know what level they (central bank) would like the dollar to reach before they come in," one dealer said.

He and other dealers were however agreed that the local unit's woes were not connected to a national government budget announced on Thursday, saying it contained nothing to affect the foreign exchange market in the immediate term.

At around 0830 GMT on Friday, the Zimbabwe dollar was trading at 11.4900/6000 against the U.S. dollar, little changed from 11.5000/6000 the previous day, but eased to 19.1590/2540 from 19.1305/1505 versus sterling, tracking a softer U.S. unit overseas.
It was at 6.2640/2880 from 6.2230/2300 against the mark and at 2.5315/5425 on the rand from 2.5050/5105.
